uzo.purpose: Leads between the main pages of an application and shows where the person is.

instead.kialo: One link is a ligilo, because a navigation is a list of places with one marked as the current; a single destination has no list and no current.
Views of the same thing on one page are tabs, because the person stays where they are; a navigation leaves the page.
The steps of a process are no menu, because their order is the process and a person may not skip ahead; Fundamento has no step indicator yet, a person decides.

boundary.kialo: A second level that opens under an item is a menu with its own keyboard, because the person moves in two directions; a person decides whether a second navigation on the page does it.

A collapsed navigation needs an overlay with a keyboard of its own (open, close, trap the focus), because the items are hidden until asked for; a navigation that wraps stays visible and needs none of it.
A breadcrumb shows the path to the page, not the pages beside it, because its items are the ancestors in order; that is the spuro (Spec 015 ① closes the boundary breadcrumb).

containers.name: shell
containers.kialo: A navigation stands in the shell of the application — the region nav of the sxelo — because it belongs to every page and to none.

with.kialo: Its items are links, because each one moves to a page and none acts here.
A count next to an item is an insigno with intent info and a description, because the digit alone says nothing (1 Version in Prüfung).
